children: Bank Indonesia Executive Director of Monetary and Securities Management Erwin Hutapea said in a Thursday statement that the central bank has continued intervening through offshore nondeliverable forward foreign exchange, spot foreign exchange, and domestic nondeliverable forward transactions, as well as purchases of government bonds in the secondary market. According to Sina Finance, Bank Indonesia is also strengthening coordination and communication with companies and market participants.

The rupiah weakened amid expectations that U.S. monetary policy will tighten, concerns over global inflation and the fiscal outlook, tensions in the Middle East, and rising domestic foreign-exchange demand. Bank Indonesia said domestic pressure mainly came from importers' foreign-exchange demand at the end of the third quarter and portfolio outflows from emerging-market assets.

Bank Indonesia said it will remain in the market to ensure exchange-rate movements are in line with fundamentals and stay stable. It is also strengthening market-oriented monetary policy operations, including increasing incentives for swap and DNDF transactions, providing hedging transactions for offshore financing, and expanding the range of eligible underlying transactions.

title: Bank Indonesia Continues Market Intervention to Stabilize the Rupiah
